CAP: STARTER: South Texas AI Research, Training, and Education Resource
CONGRANT.AWARDORG: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The South Texas AI Research, Training, and Education Resource (STARTER) will lay the foundations for long-term growth in AI-powered research across multiple disciplines and interdisciplinary centers of research at the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV). STARTER will implement a capacity building plan that provides (i) computing infrastructure, (ii) AI-related education and training, and (iii)technical expertise in AI tools and high performance computing. In close collaboration with STARTER,existing and new research projects will leverage these resources to significantly enhance their competitiveness. Concrete outreach initiatives include AI-related summer research projects for high school and community college students. Collectively, these activities will foster a community of active AI practitioners to drive a sustainable expansion of institutional AI capacity.

CONGRANT.TITLE: FronterAi: Participatory Machine Learning to Analyze Immigration Enforcement Impacts
CONTENT_GOAL: GOAL 16: Peace and Justice Strong Institutions
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: This Level 1 NEH Digital Humanities Advancement project seeks to utilize the method of community-based, participatory machine-learning to develop a novel, open-source computational tool for studying, understanding and analyzing impacts of immigration enforcement on outcomes of well-being on border communities, including: (a) quality of life, (b) health and safety, and (c) individual rights and privacy. The product of the project will be a platform called FronterAi, an open-source generative AI chatbot and analytics dashboard on immigration enforcement impacts hosted through the Machine Intelligence Lab at UTRGV and made publicly available on the Border Studies Archive. The platform will be designed with community participants to be used by both digital humanities scholars and researchers, as well as community organizations to understand, analyze and solve local problems concerning relationships between immigration enforcement and community narratives of daily life on the border.

CONGRANT.TITLE: DSC: Data Science Mastery Program (DSMP)
Center for Epistemic Justice in Artificial Intelligence
CONTENT_GOAL: GOAL 16: Peace and Justice Strong Institutions
GOAL 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: This proposal seeks funding from the National Endowment for the Humanities to establish the Center for Epistemic Justice in Artificial Intelligence (CEJAI) at UTRGV. The center will critically examine how AI intersects with epistemic justice, focusing on marginalized communities, particularly in the US-Mexico borderlands. Drawing from the works of Miranda Fricker, Kristie Dotson, and Gloria Anzaldúa, CEJAI will explore how AI systems shape social knowledge production, addressing systemic inequities and reinforcing democratic values in technology. Through interdisciplinary collaboration between the humanities, sciences, and engineering, the center aims to develop inclusive frameworks and participatory approaches for AI development, aligning with NEH goals to integrate ethical and cultural dimensions into the study of emerging technologies.

CONGRANT.TITLE: MRI: Acquisition of a GPU-Accelerated Cluster, High Performance Rio Grande Valley Cluster (HiRGV)
Faculty Seed Research Grant
CONGRANT.AWARDORG: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Measuring teaching performance is a key indicator to assess teaching quality because teaching behaviors reflect how well teachers understand subject matter, design learning tasks for students, are equipped with strategies for facilitating learning, and implement the designed learning tasks to class. When it comes to implementing a lesson plan, gathering students’ attention is the first step in implementing the lesson plan to help students process information about a subject topic. Efficient delivery of a concept maximizes learning experiences. Although we recognize the importance of evaluating teaching performance, evaluating teaching performance is costly. Especially, analyzing teaching behaviors in research takes painful efforts and needs arduous manual work, since it includes video recording, developing rubrics, transcribing, coding various teaching behaviors including verbal and nonverbal behaviors, analyzing the data, and so forth. Aligned with data-driven empirical studies, this study seeks an innovative way to calibrate teaching quality by analyzing teaching behaviors with deep learning supported by Artificial Intelligence (AI). Here, from a multidisciplinary approach based on theories in cognition, learning sciences, and computer sciences, we attempt to build an AI-driven system which calibrates teaching quality by analyzing teachers’ behaviors that help students deeply engage in learning. An AI system will be trained based on machine learning algorithms and the data obtained from the system will be cross-checked with the findings from manual coding to test and secure the system’s reliability. This automated system makes an attempt to build one of the first tools that analyze teaching behaviors driven by AI. The findings from the project will lay a foundation to measure various teaching behaviors for classroom orchestration and learning behaviors more accurately and efficiently.

Storm Surge Flood Maps Development for the Lower Laguna Madre Coastal Emergency Management
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
Hurricane storm surge is an abnormal rise in sea level that destroys coastal lands due to the extensive eroding caused by the rapid flow circulation of a hurricane, as well as overland floods caused by the abnormal rise in the ocean. The storm surge is a definite threat to the Lower Laguna Madre (LLM), though it was fortunately spared by Hurricane Harvey. LLM plays a significant role as part of the United State Gulf Intracoastal Waterway by providing tourist attraction and natural habitats for marine life. A storm surge will not only damage the natural and man-made environment, but will impair the Texas economy as well.

To fill the information gap regarding the impact of a hurricane storm surge on coastal inundation, we need more accurate and realistic prediction of storm surge flood event. We propose coupling the hurricane storm surge and watershed flood models by using the storm surge heights computed by the storm surge model as input data to the watershed flood model. The major outcomes of this proposed project consist of (1) improved coastal flood interactive GIS maps incorporating hurricane storm surge, (2) coupled hydrodynamic model to be used for the LLM hurricane storm surge and flow circulation prediction, and (3) improved local emergency evacuation routes based on coastal flood maps. The immediate benefit of these outcomes to the end-users are (1) high fidelity coastal flood geospatial information that will serve as an effective tool for local emergency management and planning and (2) robust numerical models that will be applicable to flow circulation prediction, flood routing, and traffic capacity simulation.

CONGRANT.TITLE: System for Predicting South Padre Island shoreline Erosion
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: We propose developing a numerical prediction system to estimate shoreline changes and dune erosion impacted by time scales of coastal storm events and arbitrary geometry alterations for coastal infrastructures.  The system will compute coastal morphodynamic processes of ocean sediment transport, sand dune deformation, and cross sectional profile changes.  The processes will be estimated based on hydrodynamic model computations of short/long wave transformation and dynamic currents, as well as hurricane storm surge and coastal inundation.  We are proposing to build the morphodynamic computational model by using the XBeach model, which is a public domain numerical code developed by open source community with major funding from U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, UNESCO-IHE, and Deltares.  With existing supports of the TGLO CMP #23 program, we will develop the hydrodynamic model of the South Padre Island vicinity area. To improve the modeling efficiency, we will couple the XBeach coastal morphodynamic model with the hydrodynamic model.  The coupled model will maximize computational accuracy of shoreline changes and dune erosion during hurricane storm surge along the 32.2 miles of South Padre Island.

CONGRANT.TITLE: ISAR SIMULATION AND RECOGNITION FOR A THREE DIMENSIONAL HYBRID MATERIAL TARGET
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Automatic target recognition (ATR) system based on the machine learning technology can automatically extract features from a moving target using its inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) images for high-speed target. However, ATR systems have not been applied for the widespread use in high-speed weapon system due to the difficulty in evolving to learn to recognize new targets.  This requires significant amounts of measured training data and/or high-fidelity models. In this project, we propose fast target recognition based on efficient ISAR image classification methods using ISAR image generated from the realistic 3D moving target model. It consists of three modules, multiple mono-static and/or bi-static ISAR imaging, 3D reconstruction for radar images, and complex valued 3D convolutional neural network.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Machine-Learning-Based Model for Hurricane Storm Surge Forecasting in the Lower Laguna Madre
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Algorithms
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: During every Atlantic hurricane season, storms represent a constant risk to Texan coastalcommunities and other communities along the Atlantic coast of the United States. A storm surgerefers to the abnormal rise of sea water level due to hurricanes and storms; traditionally, hurricanestorm surge predictions are generated using complex numerical models that require high amountsof computing power to be run, which grow proportionally with the extent of the area covered bythe model. In this work, a machine-learning-based storm surge forecasting model for the LowerLaguna Madre is implemented. The model considers gridded forecasted weather data on windsand atmospheric pressure over the Gulf of Mexico, as well as previous sea levels obtained from aLaguna Madre ocean circulation numerical model. Using architectures such as Convolutional NeuralNetworks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) combined, the resulting model is capableof identifying upcoming hurricanes and predicting storm surges, as well as normal conditions inseveral locations along the Lower Laguna Madre. Overall, the model is able to predict storm surgepeaks with an average difference of 0.04 m when compared with a numerical model and an averageRMSE of 0.08 for normal conditions and 0.09 for storm surge conditions.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Storm Surge Flood Maps Development for the Lower Laguna Madre Coastal Emergency Management
Automation and coupling of models for coastal flood forecasting in South Texas
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: International Journal of Ocean and Coastal Engineering/World Scientific Publishing
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Forecasting of natural disasters such as inundations can be of great help for emergency bodies and first responders. In coastal communities, this risk is often associated with storm surge. To produce flood forecasts for coastal communities a system must incorporate models capable of simulating such events based on forecasted weather conditions. In this work, a system for forecasting inundations based predominantly on storm surge is explored. An automation and coupling strategy were implemented to produce forecasted flood maps automatically. The system leverages an ocean circulation model and a channel water flow model to estimate flood events in South Texas specially alongside the Lower Laguna Madre. The system around the models is implemented using Python and the meteorological forcing input is obtained from weather forecasting models maintained by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). The forecasted weather data retrieval, data processing and automation of the models is successful, and the complete stack of software can be deployed locally or in cloud solutions to accelerate computations. The resulting system performs as expected and successfully produces flood maps automatically.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Real-Time Road Hazard Information System
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Infrastructures/MDPI
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Infrastructure is a significant factor in economic growth for systems of government. In order to increase economic productivity, maintaining infrastructure quality is essential. One of the elements of infrastructure is roads. Roads are means which help local and national economies be more productive. Furthermore, road damage such as potholes, debris, or cracks is kin to many on-road accidents that have cost the lives of many drivers. In this paper, we propose a system that uses Convolutional Neural Networks to detect road degradations without data pre-processing. We utilize the state-of-the-art object detection algorithm, YOLO detector for the system. First, we developed a basic system working on data collecting, pre-processing, and classification. Secondly, we improved the classification performance achieving 97.98% in the overall model testing, and then we utilized pixel-level classification and detection with a method called semantic segmentation. We were able to achieve decent results using this method to detect and classify four different classes (Manhole, Pothole, Blurred Crosswalk, Blurred Street Line). We trained a segmentation model that recognizes the four classes mentioned above and achieved great results with this model allowing the machine to effectively and correctly identify and classify our four classes in an image. Although we obtained excellent accuracy from the detectors, these do not perform particularly well on embedded systems due to their network size. Therefore we opted for a smaller, less accurate detector that will run in real-time on a cheap embedded system, like the Google Coral Dev Board, without needing a powerful and expensive GPU.

PRESENT.TITLE: Coastal Storm Surge Inundation Forecasting Map Automation and Coupling
PRESENT.ABSTRACT: The prediction of inundations due to hurricane storm surge can be of great help for first responders andthe general public. The accurate forecast of inundations will require a system capable of working 24/7,have high standards of reliability and be stable. In case of a storm event the forecasting system willprovide a reliable and accurate data source for flooding maps. A flood forecasting system requires thelatest forecasting data regarding wind speed, direction and surface level pressure. The forecasting datathat will be used in this project is obtained from NOAA, more specifically, from the North AmericanMesoscale Forecasting System (NAM); a model that produces gridded forecasting data over NorthAmerica. The retrieved data from NAM needs to be processed before it can be used. The gridded dataneeds to be trimmed, interpolated onto a regular grid and processed to fit the input parameters for themodels involved. The models used for inundation prediction need to be coupled and automated to fitthe requirements of the project. The models that will be used are ADCIRC and HEC-RAS. These models,when coupled, will output the necessary data to create flooding maps. This data needs to be handledand superimposed onto an interactive base GIS map, which will be available for the public to access.The system will be constructed using popular tools for data processing and automation built on Python. In this way,the public will possess reliable forecasting flood maps and will be able to plan their actions ahead of unpredictable catastrophic disasters.
